chunks: 5066 - And in the narration of Wahb ibn Wahb, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام:

“Indeed, ʿAlī عليه السلام would not administer the legal punishment in the case of insinuation until one came with an explicit slanderous accusation, such as: ‘O adulterer,’ or ‘O son of an adulteress,’ or ‘You are not your father’s son.’”

key_terms.الزَّانِيَةِ: adulteress; a woman accused of illicit sexual conduct
key_terms.زَانِ: adulterer or fornicator as a direct insult
key_terms.لِأَبِيكَ: belonging to your father, here in the context of denying paternity
key_terms.يَحُدُّ: to administer the prescribed legal punishment

ai.seo_question: When is the legal punishment for slander applied in cases of indirect accusation?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام did not impose the hadd punishment for mere insinuation unless the accusation of illicit sexual misconduct was stated clearly and explicitly. It highlights a judicial standard in slander cases, requiring unambiguous wording before the legal punishment is applied.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5066 - In the narration of Wahb ibn Wahb from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as):

"Indeed, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) would not administer the legal punishment for insinuation unless it was a clear and explicit accusation, such as saying, 'O' adulterer,' or 'O' son of an adulteress,' or 'You are not your father's son.'"
